channel.title: Nathan Moore — Insights
channel.description: Practical website notes for lean B2B marketing teams.

item.title: Agency, contractor, or in-house: who should own your B2B website?
item.description: Choose a website agency, independent partner, or in-house hire by matching your backlog, coordination needs, and ongoing responsibilities to the right model.

item.title: Your first 30 days with an inherited B2B website
item.description: A first-month plan for marketing leaders inheriting a website: establish access, test the inquiry path, preserve evidence, and choose a useful first fix.

item.title: A B2B website brief that makes launch more predictable
item.description: Build a website brief around buyer decisions, approved claims, scope boundaries, dependencies, and acceptance criteria so your team can plan a realistic launch.

item.title: When an interactive product demo earns its place on a B2B website
item.description: Decide whether an interactive product demo will clarify a buyer's question, then scope the interaction, accessible alternatives, maintenance, and measurement.

item.title: A B2B landing-page checklist for the complete inquiry path
item.description: Review the full path from campaign promise to sales handoff, including proof, calls to action, form fields, errors, confirmations, and inquiry ownership.

item.title: SEO and AI search: what a lean B2B team should prioritize
item.description: Prioritize useful B2B content, technical access, truthful evidence, and defensible measurement using current Google guidance for search and generative AI.

item.title: How to measure a low-traffic B2B website without inventing an A/B-test winner
item.description: Use counts, qualified inquiries, usability evidence, and clear decision rules to improve a low-traffic B2B website without overstating small-sample results.

item.title: What a B2B website retainer should include
item.description: Define a website retainer with clear capacity, priorities, response expectations, maintenance duties, and acceptance criteria for manageable recurring work.

item.title: How to write a B2B comparison page a buyer can actually use
item.description: Create a credible B2B comparison page with buyer-led criteria, current sources, qualified claims, explicit tradeoffs, and a practical evaluation plan.

item.title: A website launch QA guide for B2B marketing leaders
item.description: Plan a practical B2B website launch review covering forms, analytics, accessibility, mobile behavior, content accuracy, release ownership, and recovery.
